audit.process: ledger — delegated development, migrations and deployment
audit.scope: ledger repo: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/, Makefile, tools/, deploy/, .github/workflows/, .golangci.yml, internal/adapters/httpapi (guardrail), .harness/

resolved.how: tools/localdb called at the head of migrate and reset-db; TestMakeTargetsRefuseRemote seen red on the old Makefile (psql called with the staging URL), green afterwards. No override: docs/operations.md says staging and production only go through deploy.yml.

elements.finding: Fixed on 2026-11-14 (was P1): reset-db and migrate only checked the presence of DATABASE_URL, not the target; the forbidden item "local database only" existed only in AGENTS.md, although it was born of a loss of QA data on staging.
elements.target: Both targets refuse (exit 1, typed message) a DATABASE_URL whose host is not local (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, Unix socket), unless an explicit override variable is set; the refusal is tested.
elements.check: `DATABASE_URL=postgres://u@staging.example/ledger_staging make reset-db` exits with 1 without calling psql; with localhost the target runs.

elements.finding: The lint job carries the rule "no float for an amount" (forbidigo) but runs in continue-on-error: the rule is not held, and internal/app/fees.go already violates it.
elements.target: Fix fees.go with integer arithmetic, then a blocking job (or a test) limited to forbidigo on internal/domain and internal/app, independent of the debt of the other linters.
elements.check: A float64 added in internal/app makes a required check fail; fees.go no longer contains a float; TestOpenAccountAndQuote stays green (1000 → 15).

elements.finding: The rule "replayed response → Idempotency-Replayed: true", confirmed by the owner and used by the mobile app, is neither implemented (POST /transfers) nor tested.
elements.target: The use case signals the replay, the handler sets the header; a test walks routes() like idempotency_guard_test.go and requires the header on the second call of every non-exempt write route.
elements.check: The test fails on the current code (POST /transfers replayed without the header), then passes.

elements.finding: "The key is looked up inside the write transaction" is only checked by the review: the only SQL test is a round trip, it does not run in CI, and it cannot run at all (no pgx driver in go.mod).
elements.target: A CI job with a migrated PostgreSQL service that runs the integration tests, including a test of two concurrent transfers with the same key that requires a single debit.
elements.check: The job runs on every PR touching internal/adapters/postgres or internal/app; the concurrent test fails if the lookup is moved out of the transaction.

elements.finding: The owner cites test and arch as the only checks that block the merge: the migrations job does not appear as required, and it only runs on PRs; a red one can therefore be merged.
elements.target: The migrations job is a required check of the protection of main (like test and arch).
elements.check: A PR that modifies migrations/0001_accounts.sql is red and cannot be merged.

elements.finding: dry_run is true by default (healthy), but nothing in the repository prevents running the workflow from an unmerged branch with dry_run=false: its migrations, which never went through migrationcheck, would go to the shared staging database; the environment protections cannot be read and the owner did not confirm them.
elements.target: A step that fails if github.ref is not refs/heads/main when dry_run is false; staging and production environments limited to main, production with a required reviewer.
elements.check: A dispatch from another branch with dry_run=false fails before apply.sh; the environment settings are confirmed in writing.

elements.finding: The plan is JSON (healthy), but "migrations" counts every file whereas the header announces the pending migrations: a reviewer can be mistaken about what will be applied.
elements.target: Rename the field (migrations_total) or really compute the pending migrations.
elements.check: The field says what it counts.

elements.finding: README announces `make e2e`, a target missing from the Makefile: an agent that runs it fails.
elements.target: Remove the line (or create the target if it exists elsewhere).
elements.check: Every command of the README exists.

elements.finding: 33 lines, declared mode, dated and justified rules, leaks marked "(unverified)", maintenance clause; one forbidden line duplicates a rule.
elements.target: Unchanged, apart from the removal of AGENTS.md:26.

elements.finding: Tested guardrail, -json output, exit 1: carries the layers rule.
Walks the single list of routes, exemption justified and checked: carries the presence of the key.
Tested tool, exit 1 on any entry that is not an addition; its weakness is the job that calls it (see ci-migrations).
forbidigo rule citing ADR 0002; its weakness is the non-blocking job (see ci-lint).
Called only by deploy.yml, secret held in L4, JSON output, idempotent migrations (IF NOT EXISTS).
ADRs, post-mortem and operations give the why of the rules; loaded on demand.
Generic human conventions, not loaded by the agent: no context cost.
Target 3, today's harvest marker with no signal yet: nothing collected without follow-up.

process_leaks.guard_tool: guard step github.ref == main in deploy.yml + environment protections

process_leaks.rule: No float for an amount in internal/domain and internal/app
process_leaks.if_skipped: rounding errors that distort a balance (ADR 0002)
process_leaks.guard_tool: forbidigo as a blocking job, limited to internal/domain and internal/app

process_leaks.if_skipped: the mobile app shows two confirmations
process_leaks.guard_tool: httpapi test that walks routes() and replays each write

process_leaks.rule: Idempotency key looked up inside the write transaction
process_leaks.guard_tool: concurrent PostgreSQL integration test in CI

process_leaks.rule: An applied migration is never modified again (guardrail present, check not required)
process_leaks.if_skipped: staging and production diverge from the repository's schema
process_leaks.guard_tool: migrations job as a required check on main

guarded_rules.rule: Domain with no dependency, use cases → ports, independent adapters
Every non-GET route requires Idempotency-Key (presence only)
make reset-db / make migrate only on your own local database
guarded_rules.guarded_by: tools/localdb called by the Makefile targets; tools/localdb/main_test.go (job test, blocking), added on 2026-11-14

removals.text: Modifying an existing file of `migrations/`. … Enforced by: tools/migrationcheck
removals.evidence: duplicate of the rule AGENTS.md:21, same guardrail

owner_questions: 1. What protections do the GitHub staging and production environments have (reviewers, branches limited to main)? Default: none taken for granted, github.ref guard in deploy.yml.
2. Is the migrations job a required check on main? Default: no, make it required.
3. Which hosts count as a "local database" for reset-db/migrate? Default: localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 and Unix socket, with an explicit override ALLOW_REMOTE_DB=1 reserved for deploy.
4. Must the integer fee keep the current rounding (to nearest, half up)? Default: yes, (cents*15+500)/1000.

remediation.action: Add to the reset-db and migrate targets a guard that refuses a non-local host (exit 1), tested.
remediation.check: reset-db with a staging URL exits with 1 without calling psql; then AGENTS.md:24 is reduced to its "Enforced by" line.

remediation.action: Guard step github.ref == refs/heads/main when dry_run is false; confirm the environment protections.
remediation.check: Dispatch from a branch with dry_run=false fails before apply.sh.

remediation.action: Make the migrations job required in the protection of main.
remediation.check: A PR that modifies an existing migration cannot be merged.

remediation.action: Rewrite fees.go with integers, then a blocking forbidigo job limited to internal/domain and internal/app.
remediation.check: A float64 added in internal/app makes the PR red and unmergeable.

remediation.action: Replay test on every write route, then the header on POST /transfers.
remediation.check: Test seen red on the current code, then green.

remediation.action: Add the pgx driver, a PostgreSQL CI job and a test of concurrent transfers with the same key.
remediation.check: The job runs on PRs and fails if the lookup leaves the transaction.
Every command of the README exists.

remediation.action: Rename the migrations field to migrations_total, or compute the pending migrations.
remediation.check: The field says what it counts.
The migrations rule appears only once.
